title: Read Shell Midden (15Bt10), Butler County
summary: In Butler County, the Read Shell Midden is a Late Archaic camp and cemetery dug by WPA crews from 1937 to 1939, with more than 240 burials found.
bodyMarkdown:
In Butler County, the Read Shell Midden is another Late Archaic (roughly 3000–1000 BCE) camp-and-cemetery in the same shell-midden world as other Late Archaic sites in Kentucky. WPA crews dug it from 1937 to 1939 under William S. Webb; more than 240 burials were identified, though poor preservation left only about 152 individuals removable for study. Webb’s 1950 report and later paleodemography treat Read as seasonal habitation plus mortuary ground.

It joined the National Register in 1986 with a thematic group of Archaic shell middens—Kentucky’s densest Archaic shell-midden landscape.
Source: [https://npgallery.nps.gov/AssetDetail/NRIS/86000647](https://npgallery.nps.gov/AssetDetail/NRIS/86000647)
